summary: At just 187 people per square mile spread across 29 square miles, Palermo is less a town and more a loose constellation of properties scattered across the flat agricultural plain of Butte County, a few miles south of Oroville and about 70 miles north of Sacramento. The landscape here is Sacramento Valley floor — open-sky horizons, olive and citrus orchards, and long views toward the Sierra Nevada foothills to the east and the Sutter Buttes to the south. With 9.2 hours of sunshine daily and an average high around 75°F, summers run genuinely hot (triple digits are routine in July and August), while winters are mild and foggy in the classic Central Valley pattern. The affordability math is striking by California standards — a median home at $287,000 against median household income of $47,893 yields a price-to-income ratio near 6:1, tight but dramatically lower than coastal metros — yet a 21% poverty rate signals that even these prices stretch many local budgets, and median rent at $1,067 claims roughly 27% of that median gross income. Employment is overwhelmingly elsewhere: Oroville and Chico absorb most commuters, with healthcare, agriculture, government, and the university in Chico forming the primary job base. There is no real commercial center — no walkable main street, no cluster of restaurants or shops — so daily errands and dining mean driving. Palermo is the kind of place where your property line is your primary amenity and the nearest trail or park requires a car, offering California sunshine and space at a fraction of coastal cost, but demanding you build your own daily routine rather than plugging into an existing one.
